hoses: Supply line from hydrant to Engine 181 intake
Attack Line A: 250 ft of 1¾-inch hose to a third-floor interior attack position
Attack Line B: 200 ft of 1¾-inch hose to a ground-level exterior attack position
sceneElements.elevation: Line A operates on the 3rd floor; Line B is at ground level

problems.title: Interior Attack Elevation
problems.question: Attack Line A is operating on the 3rd floor. For this training problem, use height = (floor number - 1) × 10 ft and 0.5 PSI/ft for elevation. What elevation pressure must be added for Line A?
problems.instructorExplanation: This question asks only for Line A's elevation component.
problems.explainMistake: Do not include hose loss or nozzle pressure when the question asks only for elevation pressure.

problems.title: Attack Line A Friction Loss
problems.question: Attack Line A is 250 ft of 1¾-inch hose flowing 185 GPM. Using C = 15.5, what is the friction loss in Attack Line A?
problems.instructorExplanation: Line A's friction loss is about 135 PSI.
problems.explainMistake: Do not add elevation or nozzle pressure to a friction-loss-only question.

problems.title: Attack Line B Friction Loss
problems.question: Attack Line B is 200 ft of 1¾-inch hose flowing 185 GPM. Using C = 15.5, what is the friction loss in Attack Line B?
problems.instructorExplanation: Line B's friction loss is about 105 PSI.
problems.explainMistake: Use Line B's 200-ft hose length, not Line A's 250-ft length.

problems.title: Governing Attack Line
problems.question: Line A is 250 ft of 1¾-inch hose flowing 185 GPM at 50 PSI to the 3rd floor. Line B is 200 ft of 1¾-inch hose flowing 185 GPM at 50 PSI at ground level. Use the stated 10 PSI training elevation allowance for Line A. Which attack line governs the pump discharge pressure?
problems.inputLabel: Enter 1 for Line A or 2 for Line B
formulaBreakdown: Line A has the higher required pressure, so enter 1.
problems.instructorExplanation: The governing-line question is scored by line number. Line A governs because it requires 195 PSI versus 155 PSI for Line B.
problems.explainMistake: Do not store or enter 195 PSI for this question; the requested answer is Line 1.

problems.title: Required Pump Discharge Pressure
problems.question: Engine 181 is supplying both lines. Line A is 250 ft of 1¾-inch hose flowing 185 GPM at 50 PSI to the 3rd floor; use the stated 10 PSI training elevation allowance. Line B is 200 ft of 1¾-inch hose flowing 185 GPM at 50 PSI at ground level. What pump discharge pressure should Engine 181 set for the governing line?
formulaBreakdown: The higher-pressure line governs, so set 195 PSI.
problems.instructorExplanation: Line A governs because it has both greater hose friction loss and the stated elevation allowance.
problems.explainMistake: Do not average the two required line pressures.
